questions.title: GATE EC 2025 | GA Question: 6
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Combinatorics deals with problems involving counting. For example, "How many distinct arrangements of $\text{N}$ distinct objects in $\text{M}$ spaces on a circle are possible?" is a typical problem in combinatorics. This kind of counting is sometimes used in the modeling of several physical phenomena. Often, in such models, the different combinatorial possibilities are assigned probability values. Assigning probabilities enables the computation of the average values of physical quantities.

Consider the following statements:

$\text{P}:$ Combinatorics is always invoked in the modeling of physical phenomena.

$\text{Q}:$ Modeling some physical phenomena involves assigning probabilities to combinatorial possibilities in order to compute average values of physical quantities.

Based on the passage above, what can be inferred about statements $\textbf{P}$ and $\textbf{Q}?$

questions.title: GATE EC 2025 | GA Question: 9
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
In the $2020$ summer Olympics' Javelin throw finals, Neeraj Chopra exhibited a spectacular performance to win the gold medal. The silver medal was won by Jakub Vadlejch and the bronze medal was won by Vitezlav Vesely. There were six rounds of throws with each athlete having one throw per round. The best of all the throws of each athlete is considered for the medal. Following were the observations about the throws:

  1. The first and second rounds were dominated by Neeraj Chopra with a gold medal performance in his second throw, while the other two athletes did not have any medal winning throws in these rounds.
  2. The throws in the last round by both Jakub Vadlejch and Vitezlav Vesely were fouls and were not considered for scoring.
  3. After four rounds, Vitezlav Vesely was in the second position and could not improve upon his best throw in the succeeding rounds.
  4. In the fourth round, the throw by Jakub Vadlejch was the best in that round.

In which round did Vitezlav Vesely have his best throw?

questions.title: GATE EC 2025 | EC Question: 1
questions.subject: Network Theory
questions.question: For a reciprocal two-port network, the condition satisfied by its transmission (ABCD) matrix parameters is:
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Network Theory):

By definition of reciprocity in transmission parameter representation, the determinant of the ABCD matrix equals unity: $\det(T) = A D - B C = 1$. The symmetry condition is $A = D$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2025 | EC Question: 9
questions.subject: Electronic Devices (EDC)
questions.question: The Einstein relation relating carrier diffusion coefficient $D$ and carrier mobility $\mu$ in a semiconductor at thermal equilibrium temperature $T$ is:
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Electronic Devices (EDC)):

Einstein's relation: $\frac{D_n}{\mu_n} = \frac{D_p}{\mu_p} = \frac{k T}{q} = V_t$ (thermal voltage $\approx 26\text{ mV}$ at $300\text{ K}$).

questions.title: GATE EC 2025 | EC Question: 16
questions.subject: Analog Circuits
questions.question: A common-emitter BJT amplifier with unbypassed emitter resistor $R_E$ introduces negative feedback that results in:
options: Increased input resistance and stabilized voltage gain
Decreased input resistance and increased voltage gain
Zero output resistance and unstable gain

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: Increased input resistance and stabilized voltage gain
structuredOptions.html: Increased input resistance and stabilized voltage gain

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: Decreased input resistance and increased voltage gain
structuredOptions.html: Decreased input resistance and increased voltage gain

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Zero output resistance and unstable gain
structuredOptions.html: Zero output resistance and unstable gain

questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Analog Circuits):

An unbypassed $R_E$ provides series-series negative feedback. This raises the input impedance ($R_{\text{in}} \approx r_\pi + (1+\beta)R_E$), stabilizes gain against $h_{fe}$ variations, and widens bandwidth.

questions.title: GATE EC 2025 | EC Question: 24
questions.subject: Digital Circuits
questions.question: The minimum number of 2-to-1 multiplexers required to realize an arbitrary 4-to-1 multiplexer without any external logic gates is:
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Digital Circuits):

A 4-to-1 multiplexer has 2 select lines. Two 2-to-1 MUXes are used in the first stage driven by $S_0$, and one 2-to-1 MUX is used in the second stage driven by $S_1$. Total MUX count $= 2 + 1 = 3$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2025 | EC Question: 26

questions.question: A linear bilateral DC network has an open-circuit voltage $V_{\text{th}} = 30\text{ V}$ and short-circuit current $I_{\text{sc}} = 5\text{ A}$ across terminals A and B. The Thevenin equivalent resistance $R_{\text{th}}$ (in Ohms) is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Network Theory):

questions.title: GATE EC 2025 | EC Question: 33
questions.subject: Electronic Devices (EDC)
questions.question: An abrupt Silicon $p\text{-}n$ junction has built-in potential $V_{bi} = 0.8\text{ V}$. The transition capacitance at zero bias is $C_{j0} = 20\text{ pF}$. When reverse biased with $V_R = 3.2\text{ V}$, the junction capacitance $C_j = \frac{C_{j0}}{\sqrt{1 + V_R / V_{bi}}}$ (in $\text{pF}$) is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Electronic Devices (EDC)):

$C_j = \frac{20}{\sqrt{1 + 3.2/0.8}} = \frac{20}{\sqrt{1 + 4}} = \frac{20}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{20}{2.236} \approx 8.94\text{ pF}$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2025 | EC Question: 41
questions.subject: Analog Circuits
questions.question: A non-inverting operational amplifier circuit has $R_1 = 5\,\text{k}\Omega$ connected from the inverting pin to ground and feedback resistor $R_f = 45\,\text{k}\Omega$. The closed-loop voltage gain $A_v = 1 + \frac{R_f}{R_1}$ is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Analog Circuits):

$A_v = 1 + \frac{R_f}{R_1} = 1 + \frac{45}{5} = 1 + 9 = 10.0$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2025 | EC Question: 48
questions.subject: Digital Circuits
questions.question: A mod-16 ripple counter is built using 4 toggle ($T$) flip-flops. If the input clock frequency is $32\text{ kHz}$, the output frequency (in $\text{kHz}$) at the final flip-flop is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Digital Circuits):

A counter with $N = 4$ flip-flops has modulus $2^N = 16$. Each flip-flop divides frequency by 2: $f_{\text{out}} = \frac{f_{\text{in}}}{16} = \frac{32\text{ kHz}}{16} = 2\text{ kHz}$.
